title: Univalence, impredicativity and propositional resizing
formal: Does there exist a nondegenerate model of ordinary dependent type theory, with the type formers and computation rules specified below, containing a univalent impredicative universe \(U\) of data types into which every homotopy proposition can be resized?

source_formulation.text: There is a natural question: can we construct a model of type theory with a univalent and impredicative universe satisfying the propositional resizing axiom?
source_formulation.caption: Complete selected source sentence; PDF p. 16

why: Determine compatibility of univalence, impredicative data-type universes and propositional resizing under ordinary dependent computation rules, clarifying a substantive boundary in foundations for proof assistants.
status_note: The ordinary-type-theory question is explicit in Uemura’s conclusion. Bounded checks on 14 September 2026 found related path-category and groupoidal models but no verified model meeting all rules specified here, nor a nonexistence theorem. Their semantic qualifications are retained; this is not an exhaustive current-openness certificate.

progress.text: Van den Berg v2 supplies related path-category universes with univalence and resizing, subject to the semantic and coherence qualifications of that setting.
The TYPES 2018 proceedings publish Uemura’s model and resizing failure, retaining the question for ordinary type theory.
Speight’s groupoidal model provides impredicativity without general function extensionality; it does not supply all structures required here.

importance.reason: A focused foundational compatibility question connecting universe polymorphism, homotopical equality and proof-assistant semantics. Known models separately support substantial parts of the specification, while their computation-rule and resizing distinctions make the remaining target meaningful; it is narrower than a general consistency problem for type theory.

sentences: An impredicative universe supports quantification over types without the usual increase in universe size, while univalence connects equivalence with equality.
Propositional resizing adds the requirement that large propositions have equivalent small representatives.
The source asks for a model of type theory supporting all three features together.
Its cubical assembly construction provides univalence and impredicativity but fails resizing, and a related positive model weakens identity and dependent-product structure.

Constructing a model with the intended ordinary type-theoretic rules would clarify whether these attractive foundational principles can coexist without sacrificing essential forms of dependent reasoning.

definitions: A model is a set-based category with families: it has contexts and substitutions forming a category with an empty terminal context, types over each context, terms of each type, and context extension \(\Gamma.A\) classifying a substitution into \(\Gamma\) together with a term of its reindexed type \(A\). Reindexing of types and terms obeys identity and composition strictly. Type-forming operations, constructors and eliminators commute strictly with reindexing. Require dependent products \(\prod_{x:A}B(x)\), dependent sums \(\sum_{x:A}B(x)\), intensional identity types \(\operatorname{Id}_A(a,b)\), empty and unit types, binary coproducts, and natural numbers. Products have abstraction and application with the usual judgmental beta and eta equations; sums have pairing, projections and dependent elimination with their usual computation equations. Identity types have reflexivity and the unrestricted dependent eliminator \(J\), whose reflexivity computation equation holds judgmentally. Empty, unit, coproduct and natural-number types have their usual dependent eliminators and judgmental constructor equations. Also require function extensionality: the canonical map from an identity of dependent functions to their pointwise identities is an equivalence. Judgmental equations are equalities of the interpreted operations, rather than merely inhabited identity types. Nondegenerate means that the interpreted empty type has no closed term. A Tarski universe is an ambient type \(U\) with a decoding family \(\operatorname{El}:U\to\mathrm{Type}\). It has codes for empty, unit, binary coproduct and natural-number types and is closed under dependent sums and identity types of decoded small types. It is impredicative when, for every ambient type \(A\) and family \(b:A\to U\), the dependent product \(\prod_{x:A}\operatorname{El}(b(x))\) has a code in \(U\). These coding operations and their decoding identifications must be specified and stable under substitution; decoded closure may hold up to specified isomorphism. The domain \(A\) need not itself have a code in \(U\). There is no requirement that \(U\) code itself. Write \(\operatorname{isProp}(P)=\prod_{x,y:P}\operatorname{Id}_P(x,y)\). A type is contractible if it has a point identified with every point; a map is an equivalence if every fiber \(\sum_x\operatorname{Id}(f(x),y)\) is contractible. Univalence means that, for all \(a,b:U\), the canonical transport map \(\operatorname{Id}_U(a,b)\to\operatorname{Equiv}(\operatorname{El}(a),\operatorname{El}(b))\) is an equivalence. Propositional resizing means that for every ambient type \(P\), in every context with a term of \(\operatorname{isProp}(P)\), there is a small proposition code \(p:U\) and an equivalence \(P\simeq\operatorname{El}(p)\), uniformly under substitution. These are internal structures of the model; external equivalence of isolated fibers is insufficient. No particular assembly, cubical or path-category presentation, no Church’s thesis and no higher inductive types are required.
answer_criterion: Give a complete mathematically correct proof checked in Lean that such a model exists, specifying its semantic structures and verifying all rules, closure, univalence, resizing and nondegeneracy; or prove in Lean that no such model exists. A merely postulated model, a model with only propositional universes, or a model validating only weaker identity or dependent-product computation rules does not satisfy this formulation. A failure of resizing in one candidate model is not a universal nonexistence proof.

context_blocks.text: A universe is a type whose elements name other types. Ordinary predicative universes generally move to a larger level when one quantifies over a larger domain. Impredicativity instead keeps a product small whenever its values are small, even if the domain is large. Here the universe includes natural numbers and other data types; it is not only a collection of propositions.

Univalence says that equivalent small types are identified in the universe, with the appropriate higher identity structure. Resizing asks a different question: whether every ambient proposition already has a small representative. A proposition is a type whose any two inhabitants are identified, which does not require it to have an inhabitant.

Uemura constructs a cubical assembly model with a univalent impredicative universe and proves that resizing into that universe fails. His concluding question asks for compatibility of the three principles in another model, rather than for a proof of resizing in the displayed countermodel.

This card spells out the ordinary-type-theory reading of that question. The data-type codes and nondegeneracy prevent a vacuous or proposition-only interpretation; strict substitution and the stated computation rules specify the coherence demanded of a model. It does not add a requirement for a particular semantic construction.

Van den Berg gives related positive path-category constructions, including an impredicative univalent universe of sets with resizing. Uemura explicitly distinguishes their weaker identity and dependent-product structure from a model of ordinary homotopy type theory. Those positive results therefore need their semantic qualification when compared with this target.

Speight’s later groupoidal realizability work constructs an impredicative universe of 1-types, but the model does not validate function extensionality in general. Its concluding questions still distinguish univalent universes and resizing. The presence of an impredicative universe alone does not supply the full structure requested here.

A resolution would clarify whether a universe supporting ordinary data, equivalence-based identity and quantification over larger domains can coexist with small representatives for all propositions. This affects the foundations of dependent reasoning and proof-assistant universe systems, rather than the runtime of a program.
